about: Curated questions for 'Ask the evidence' (REVIEW_ISSUES R06c; AI_FIRST_PLAN.md). Answers and paraphrases written with Claude Code from pipeline/ai/context.md only; every sentence is checked by pipeline/ai_build.mjs. Paraphrases only help match a visitor's wording (pipeline/embed.mjs).

questions.question: Has any solid fuel been tested above 30% oxygen?

answer.text: No. The highest oxygen level in any solid-fuel data table in PSI is 22.2%, in BASS-II.
Of the 270 runs at 30% oxygen or more, all come from gas flames (ACME Flame Design, ACME CFI-G) or fuel droplets (FLEX).
The closest evidence for materials is ACME BRE, a gas burner that emulates burning solids: its flames kept burning without airflow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres but went out at 21% oxygen.

paraphrases: Have materials been burned at high oxygen levels in space?
Is there solid fuel data above 30 percent oxygen?
What is the highest oxygen any burning material was tested at?

questions.question: Does shutting off ventilation put a fire out in microgravity?

answer.text: Not reliably. ACME BRE saw flames emulating PMMA and Nylon keep burning steadily with no airflow, even though stopping ventilation is an established step in fighting spacecraft fires.
That held in elevated-oxygen atmospheres; at 21% oxygen the same flames went out in a short time.
BASS also found that a local suppressant jet pulled in air and kept a flame burning even with the ambient airflow turned off.

paraphrases: If the fans are turned off, does a fire go out?
Does stopping airflow extinguish a fire in space?
Will cutting the ventilation starve a fire on a spacecraft?

questions.question: Is NASA's normal-gravity flammability test conservative for space?

answer.text: Not always. NASA states that the 1-g screening test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) is not conservative, because materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.

SAFFIRE-II, the one study with matched burns in both gravities, shows it depends on the material: silicone and PMMA burned less in microgravity, while the cotton-fiberglass fabric burned its full length in both.

paraphrases: Are Earth flammability tests good enough for spacecraft materials?
Does NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 predict how materials burn in space?
Can a material pass on Earth but burn in microgravity?

questions.question: Which data supports a lunar habitat at 30% oxygen and 70.3 kPa?

answer.text: Very little. Of 875 runs with both oxygen and pressure, 23 fall within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of this atmosphere, all of them FLEX fuel droplets.
No solid-fuel table records pressure, and the highest solid-fuel oxygen is 22.2%, 7.8 points short.
None of the 19 flight investigations ran at lunar gravity.

paraphrases: What experiments match a Moon base atmosphere?
Is there fire data for a lunar habitat?
How well is a 30% oxygen, 10.2 psi Moon habitat covered by tests?

questions.question: What evidence exists for NASA's Exploration Atmosphere (34% oxygen, 56.5 kPa)?

answer.text: Only 19 runs fall within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of it, all ACME CFI-G gas flames.
FLEX-2, CFI and ACME CFI-G recorded pressure ranges that include 56.5 kPa; none of them burned solid fuels.
The highest solid-fuel oxygen tested is 11.8 points below this atmosphere.

paraphrases: Is there fire data for 34% oxygen at 8.2 psi?
Has anything been tested in the Artemis exploration atmosphere?
What experiments match NASA's exploration atmosphere?

questions.question: Is there any evidence at Moon or Mars gravity?

answer.text: No. All 19 flight investigations ran in microgravity, so there is no partial-gravity evidence in this collection.
The one gravity comparison available is SAFFIRE-II, which lists normal-gravity burn lengths next to its microgravity results.

paraphrases: Has any fire experiment run at lunar or Martian gravity?
Is there fire data at one-sixth g?
Do we know how flames behave in partial gravity?

questions.question: Would an Earth smoke detector work on a spacecraft?

answer.text: NASA says probably not as designed: smoke particles from microgravity fires differ greatly in size, so a terrestrial detector would be looking for the wrong signature.
SAME and SAME-R measured smoke from overheated spacecraft materials in the station glovebox to provide that microgravity baseline.
The first SAME flight's particle samples came back contaminated and unusable, one reason SAME-R reflew.

paraphrases: Can we use normal smoke alarms in space?
Do smoke detectors designed on Earth work in microgravity?
Why do spacecraft need different smoke detectors?

questions.question: Do gaseous suppressants work as well in space as on Earth?

answer.text: FLEX found the flammability limit is lower in microgravity, so inert-gas suppressant standards set on Earth give less margin of safety in space.
For heptane and methanol droplets, the limiting oxygen index was significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than predicted.
For burning solids, BASS found that nitrogen applied to a flame could make it stronger by drawing in oxygen.

paraphrases: Do fire extinguishing gases work in microgravity?
Is nitrogen or CO2 suppression less effective in space?
Are inert-gas fire suppression standards safe for spacecraft?

questions.question: What airflow is most dangerous for burning materials in microgravity?

answer.text: NASA states that for flame spread over solids, the lowest oxygen that supports burning occurs near 10 cm/s, the typical speed of spacecraft ventilation, where spread rate is also highest.
Direction matters too: in SAFFIRE-I at 20 cm/s, the flame spreading with the flow burned for 420 s, against the flow for 70 s.

paraphrases: At what ventilation speed do materials burn best in space?
Which air speed makes fires worst on a spacecraft?
Does ventilation airflow make fires spread faster?

questions.question: Do flames spread differently in microgravity?

answer.text: Yes. At low airflow in space, a thin fuel lit in the middle spreads its flame upstream into the oncoming air, the opposite of normal gravity.
BASS, BASS-II and the Saffire flights burned solids in both opposed and concurrent flow.

paraphrases: How do flames spread in space?
Do fires spread upstream in microgravity?
Is flame spread different without gravity?

questions.question: What are cool flames and why do they matter for fire safety?

answer.text: FLEX saw that after the visible flame around a heptane droplet went out, a stable low-temperature cool flame formed and kept burning.
NASA notes the cool flame can burn for a prolonged time, a result many researchers had thought impossible.
A fire that looks extinguished may therefore still be reacting; CFI and ACME CFI-G study cool flames in more detail.

paraphrases: What is a cool flame?
Can a fire keep burning after the flame goes out?
Why are cool flames dangerous?

questions.question: Which solid-fuel studies recorded pressure?

answer.text: None. No solid-fuel table in PSI records pressure, so FlameMap assumes cabin pressure for them and labels it as assumed.
The lowest recorded pressure in any table is 50.7 kPa, in FLEX-2 fuel-droplet tests.

paraphrases: Was pressure measured in the solid-fuel experiments?
Do we know the pressure for the material burning tests?
Which material flammability tests ran at low pressure?

questions.question: Is there any data near a spacesuit atmosphere?

answer.text: No. Of 875 runs with both oxygen and pressure, none is within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of 100% oxygen at 29.6 kPa.
The highest oxygen in any table is 40%, in gas flames, and no recorded pressure range includes 29.6 kPa.

paraphrases: Is a spacesuit a fire risk?
Has anything been burned in pure oxygen at low pressure?
Is there fire data for 100% oxygen?

questions.question: Which materials were burned in both microgravity and normal gravity?

answer.text: Only SAFFIRE-II lists both. None of its four silicone samples burned in microgravity, though two burned completely in 1-g.
Both PMMA samples burned completely in 1-g but only about 10 cm in microgravity, and the cotton-fiberglass fabric burned its full 29 cm in both.

paraphrases: Which materials were tested in both 1 g and microgravity?
Is there a direct comparison of burning on Earth and in space?
Do materials burn more in space or on Earth?

questions.question: Which studies reached the highest oxygen levels?

answer.text: Gas-flame studies: ACME BRE, ACME Flame Design and ACME CFI-G all reached 40% oxygen.

Flame Design and CFI-G were not aimed at fire safety, but they are the only runs near the oxygen levels proposed for future habitats; 37 runs reached 30% oxygen or more at 75 kPa or less, from ACME CFI-G and FLEX.

paraphrases: What is the highest oxygen level tested in any experiment?
Which experiments used high oxygen?
Has anything been burned at 40% oxygen?

questions.question: Do flames make smoke differently in low gravity?

answer.text: Yes. NASA states that gas-jet flames start producing smoke at substantially different conditions in low gravity than on Earth, contrary to earlier predictions.
SPICE measured the smoke point of gas-jet flames on the station, and SLICE reused its hardware.

paraphrases: Is soot different in microgravity?
Do flames in space produce more smoke?
How is smoke from gas flames different in low gravity?

questions.question: What did BASS-II study?
paraphrases: Tell me about BASS-II
What is the Burning and Suppression of Solids II experiment?
What were the BASS-II results?

answer.text: BASS-II burned PMMA films and sheets of several thicknesses in a small wind tunnel in the station glovebox, with flames spreading both against and with the airflow.
It varied oxygen from 13.6% to 22.2% and airflow up to 40 cm/s over 129 runs; pressure was not recorded and is assumed to be cabin pressure.
With BASS, it is the basis for NASA's statement that the 1-g material screening test is not conservative.

questions.question: What did BASS study?
paraphrases: Tell me about the BASS experiment
What is Burning and Suppression of Solids?
What did the first BASS experiment find?

answer.text: BASS burned cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex, Ultem and PMMA spheres and cylinders in a 76 mm flow duct in the station glovebox.
PSI keeps its 122 runs as a run log; oxygen and pressure were not recorded and are assumed to be cabin air.
It found that a local suppressant jet could keep a flame burning by pulling in air, and that nitrogen could strengthen a flame by drawing oxygen into it.

questions.question: What was Saffire-I?
paraphrases: Tell me about the first Saffire experiment
What happened in the Saffire-I fire test on Cygnus?
What was burned in Saffire 1?

answer.text: SAFFIRE-I burned one large cotton-fiberglass fabric sample, about 0.94 m long and 0.4 m wide, in an enclosure inside a Cygnus cargo vehicle.
At the same 20 cm/s airflow, the flame spreading with the flow burned for 420 s and the flame spreading against it for 70 s.
Pressure was not recorded and is assumed to be cabin pressure.

questions.question: What did Saffire-II test?
paraphrases: Tell me about Saffire-II
Which materials burned in the Saffire-II experiment?
What were the Saffire 2 results?

answer.text: SAFFIRE-II burned 9 samples, each 5 cm by 29 cm, of silicone, cotton-fiberglass fabric, PMMA and PMMA with Nomex in a Cygnus cargo module, at airflow of 20 to 30 cm/s.
None of the silicone samples burned in microgravity and the PMMA samples were damaged over only about 10 cm, while the fabric burned its full 29 cm.
It is the only study here that lists normal-gravity burns next to its microgravity results.

questions.question: What was Saffire-III?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Saffire-III fire experiment
What did the third Saffire flight burn?
Saffire 3 results

answer.text: SAFFIRE-III burned a large cotton-fiberglass fabric sample, 94 cm by 40.6 cm, in an enclosure inside a Cygnus cargo vehicle, at 30 cm/s airflow.
PSI holds only a partial table of 2 runs, and oxygen and pressure were not recorded; FlameMap assumes cabin air for both.

questions.question: What did SAME measure?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
What was the SAME experiment?
What smoke did SAME study?

answer.text: SAME overheated Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, lampwick and dibutyl phthalate in the station glovebox and measured the smoke with the Comparative Soot Diagnostic hardware.
Its particle samples came back contaminated and could not be used, one reason SAME-R reflew.
The aim was a microgravity baseline: smoke particles from fires in microgravity differ greatly in size from those on Earth.

questions.question: What did SAME-R measure?
paraphrases: Tell me about the SAME reflight
What is the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Reflight?
What were the SAME-R results?

answer.text: SAME-R repeated the smoke measurements, overheating Kapton, silicone, lampwick, Teflon and Pyrell foam in the station glovebox at airflow up to 8.1 cm/s.
PSI lists 109 runs in a partial table; oxygen and pressure were not recorded and are assumed to be cabin air.
It reflew partly because the first SAME flight's particle samples were contaminated.

questions.question: What was DAFT?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
What did DAFT-2 test?
What is DAFT on the space station?

answer.text: DAFT and DAFT-2 tested a TSI P-Trak particle counter on a test dust, Arizona Road Dust, held in 15-liter Mylar bags.
They measured a test dust, not smoke from a fire, and PSI keeps only a run log of 2 runs.

questions.question: What did FLEX find?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Flame Extinguishment Experiment
What was FLEX on the space station?
What did the FLEX droplet experiments show?

answer.text: FLEX burned single methanol and heptane droplets, about 1 to 5 mm across, in the Combustion Integrated Rack, at 12% to 34% oxygen and 70.2 to 309.3 kPa.
It found that the flammability limit is lower in microgravity, so inert-gas suppressant standards set on Earth leave less safety margin in space.
It also found cool flames that keep burning after the visible flame goes out.

questions.question: What did FLEX-2 study?
paraphrases: Tell me about FLEX-2
What is the Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2?
Which fuels were burned in FLEX-2?

answer.text: FLEX-2 burned droplets of iso-octane, n-octane, heptane, decane, ethanol and fuel mixtures, 1.5 to 5 mm across, in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
Its conditions span 17% to 30% oxygen, 50.7 to 304 kPa and slow airflow up to 5 cm/s; 50.7 kPa is the lowest pressure recorded in any table.
PSI lists 48 publications for it.

questions.question: What is the Cool Flames Investigation?
paraphrases: Tell me about CFI
What did the CFI experiment study?
What fuels were used in the cool flames investigation?

answer.text: CFI burned n-dodecane and n-dodecane / iso-dodecane droplets suspended on needles or fibers in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
It covered 17% to 21% oxygen and a wide pressure range, 50.7 to 506.6 kPa, over 87 runs.
It studies the cool flames that FLEX found, which can keep burning after the visible flame goes out.

questions.question: What did ACME BRE find?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Burning Rate Emulator
What is the ACME burning rate emulator experiment?
What did BRE show about burning materials?

answer.text: ACME BRE used gas flames on porous burners, 25 and 50 mm across, to emulate burning solid materials, at 21% to 40% oxygen.
Its flames emulating PMMA and Nylon kept burning with no airflow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres, but went out in a short time at 21% oxygen.
The team calls the results preliminary, but suggests NASA may want to rely more on its cone-calorimeter test.

questions.question: What was ACME Flame Design?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Flame Design experiment
What did ACME Flame Design study?
What are normal and inverse flames in ACME?

answer.text: ACME Flame Design burned spherical diffusion flames of ethylene and propane, both normal and inverse, in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
PSI lists 327 runs at 19.8% to 40% oxygen and 94.4 to 131.4 kPa.
Its runs make up 131 of the 270 runs at 30% oxygen or more.

questions.question: What did ACME CFI-G study?
paraphrases: Tell me about the cool flames investigation with gases
What is CFI-G?
Which gases were burned in ACME CFI-G?

answer.text: ACME CFI-G burned ethane, propane and butane as spherical diffusion flames, normal and inverse, to study cool flames with gaseous fuels.
PSI lists 333 runs at 18% to 40% oxygen and 50.7 to 304 kPa.
Its 19 runs are the only ones within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of NASA's Exploration Atmosphere.

questions.question: What was the ACME CLD Flame experiment?
paraphrases: Tell me about the coflow laminar diffusion flame experiment
What is CLD Flame?
What did the ACME coflow flames study?

answer.text: ACME CLD Flame burned methane and ethylene on a coflow burner in the Combustion Integrated Rack to study laminar diffusion flames.
Its partial table of 32 runs records neither oxygen nor pressure, so FlameMap counts both as untested for it.

questions.question: What was the ACME E-FIELD Flames experiment?
paraphrases: Tell me about the electric field flames experiment
Did NASA test electric fields on flames in space?
What is E-FIELD Flames?

answer.text: ACME E-FIELD Flames studied how an electric field affects methane and ethylene flames, using gas-jet and coflow burners with a mesh electrode.
Its partial table of 32 runs records neither oxygen nor pressure.

questions.question: What was ACME s-Flame?
paraphrases: Tell me about the structure and response of spherical diffusion flames
What is s-Flame?
Which fuels did s-Flame burn?

answer.text: ACME s-Flame burned hydrogen, methane and ethylene on a spherical porous burner to study the structure and response of spherical diffusion flames.
It covers 21% to 30% oxygen, but records no pressure, in a partial table of 18 runs.

questions.question: What did SPICE study?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
What did SPICE find about soot?
Which gases were burned in SPICE?

answer.text: SPICE burned methane, ethylene, propane, propylene and propylene mixtures from gas-jet nozzles of 0.41, 0.76 and 1.6 mm in a coflow duct in the station glovebox.
It studied when such flames start to produce smoke: in low gravity that happens at substantially different conditions than on Earth, and the soot particles differ in size and structure.
PSI lists 469 runs, with oxygen and pressure assumed to be cabin air.

questions.question: What did SLICE study?
paraphrases: Tell me about the Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
What was the SLICE experiment on the space station?
What gases were burned in SLICE?

answer.text: SLICE burned methane, ethylene, ethane and nitrogen-diluted mixtures from exchangeable burner tubes in a fan-driven flow duct, to study flame structure and liftoff.
PSI keeps a run log of 12 runs, so its conditions are not tabulated.
NASA's finding on smoke from gas-jet flames covers it together with SPICE: in low gravity they start producing smoke at substantially different conditions than on Earth.

questions.question: Does spraying suppressant at a flame put it out in microgravity?
paraphrases: Can a fire extinguisher jet make a fire worse in space?
Does a local extinguisher spray work on a burning sample?
Why did the BASS suppressant jets fail?

answer.text: Not in BASS and BASS-II: a suppressant jet aimed at the flame pulled in air and kept it burning, even with the ventilation airflow turned off.
Nitrogen used as the suppressant could even make the flame stronger, by drawing oxygen into it.

questions.question: Which NASA flammability test best matches microgravity flames?
paraphrases: Should NASA use the cone calorimeter test for spacecraft materials?
What is NASA Test 2 and does it matter for space?
Which material test predicts burning in microgravity?

answer.text: The ACME BRE team suggests NASA may want to rely more on its cone-calorimeter test (Test 2), which measures the material properties that matched the microgravity flames.
They call the results preliminary.
NASA also states that its 1-g screening test (Test 1) is not conservative, because materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity.

questions.question: Why did the SAME experiment fly again?
paraphrases: What went wrong with SAME?
Were the SAME smoke samples usable?
Why was there a SAME reflight?

answer.text: The particle samples from the first SAME flight could not be used: every electron-microscope grid came back contaminated with unidentified particles.
That is one reason SAME-R reflew; PSI lists 109 runs for it.

questions.question: Were there limits to what FLEX could measure?
paraphrases: Could FLEX measure droplet size at extinction?
What are the limitations of the FLEX data?
Why are some FLEX extinction sizes missing?

answer.text: Yes. In some atmospheres the droplet at flame extinction was too small to be observed or measured with the instruments on board.

questions.question: How did PMMA burn in microgravity compared with Earth?
paraphrases: Does acrylic burn less in space?
What happened to PMMA in Saffire-II?
Is PMMA more or less flammable in microgravity?

answer.text: In SAFFIRE-II, both PMMA samples burned completely in 1-g but showed only about 10 cm of significant damage in microgravity.
On one of them the flame stayed anchored at the base, and the sample regressed only 0.01 to 0.04 mm/s.
BASS-II burned PMMA films and sheets at 13.6% to 22.2% oxygen.

questions.question: Does cotton-fiberglass fabric burn in microgravity?
paraphrases: Is SIBAL fabric flammable in space?
Which material burned completely in Saffire-II?
Do fabrics burn in microgravity?

answer.text: Yes. In SAFFIRE-II, the cotton-fiberglass fabric (SIBAL) burned its full 29 cm length in microgravity, as it did in 1-g.
The same fabric was the large sample in SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III, and one of the materials in BASS.

questions.question: Do flames spreading with the airflow burn longer?
paraphrases: What is the difference between concurrent and opposed flame spread?
Does fire spread faster with or against the air on a spacecraft?
How long did the Saffire-I flames burn?

answer.text: In SAFFIRE-I at the same 20 cm/s airflow, the flame spreading with the flow (concurrent) burned for 420 s, while the flame spreading against it (opposed) burned for 70 s.
BASS-II also burned samples in both opposed and concurrent flow.

questions.question: Can fuels burn at lower oxygen in microgravity?
paraphrases: Is the limiting oxygen index lower in space?
What is the minimum oxygen for burning in microgravity?
Do droplets keep burning at lower oxygen in space?

answer.text: Yes, for droplets: FLEX found the limiting oxygen index for heptane and methanol was significantly lower than in normal gravity, and lower than predicted.
For solids, NASA states that materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity than on Earth, with the minimum near an airflow of 10 cm/s.

questions.question: Which materials burned least in microgravity?
paraphrases: Does silicone burn in microgravity?
Which spacecraft materials are least flammable in space?
Did any material refuse to burn in space?

answer.text: In SAFFIRE-II, silicone did not burn at all in microgravity and PMMA was damaged over only about 10 cm, while cotton-fiberglass fabric burned its full 29 cm.
That is one card of 9 samples in cabin air, so it says little about the higher-oxygen atmospheres planned for exploration.

questions.question: Why do fires behave differently in microgravity?
paraphrases: How is fire different in space?
Why does gravity matter for flames?
What makes fires in microgravity unusual?

answer.text: Without gravity there is no buoyant flow, so at low airflow a flame lit in the middle of a thin fuel spreads upstream into the oncoming air, the opposite of normal gravity.
Ventilation airflow then controls burning: for solids, the lowest oxygen that supports burning and the fastest spread both occur near 10 cm/s, the typical spacecraft ventilation speed.

questions.question: Which experiments studied smoke detection?
paraphrases: What fire detection research has NASA done in space?
Which studies measured smoke particles?
Are there smoke detector experiments in PSI?

answer.text: Three investigations have detection as their role: SAME, SAME-R and DAFT / DAFT-2.
SAME and SAME-R measured smoke from overheated spacecraft materials; DAFT tested a particle counter on a test dust.
SPICE and SLICE add how smoke and soot form in gas-jet flames.

questions.question: Which experiments studied fire suppression?
paraphrases: What extinguishment research exists in microgravity?
Which studies tested putting fires out?
Is there data on fire suppression in space?

answer.text: FLEX is the one investigation with suppression as its main role; FLEX-2, BASS and BASS-II list it as a secondary role.
FLEX found that inert-gas suppressant standards set on Earth give less margin in space, and BASS found that a local suppressant jet could keep a flame burning.

questions.question: Which experiments studied material flammability?
paraphrases: Which studies burned spacecraft materials?
What experiments tested how materials catch fire in space?
Which investigations are about fire prevention?

answer.text: Six investigations have prevention as their role: BASS, BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I, SAFFIRE-II, SAFFIRE-III and ACME BRE.
All but ACME BRE burned real solids; BRE used gas burners to emulate them.

questions.question: Which experiments burned liquid fuel droplets?
paraphrases: Is there data on liquid fuel fires in space?
Which studies used fuel droplets?
What liquid fuels were burned in microgravity?

answer.text: Three: FLEX (methanol and heptane), FLEX-2 (octanes, heptane, decane, ethanol and mixtures) and CFI (n-dodecane and mixtures).
Together they cover the widest pressure range in PSI, from 50.7 to 506.6 kPa.

questions.question: Which experiments burned gaseous fuels?
paraphrases: Is there data on gas fires in microgravity?
Which studies used gas flames?
What gases were burned on the space station?

answer.text: Eight: ACME BRE, ACME Flame Design, ACME CFI-G, ACME CLD Flame, ACME E-FIELD Flames, ACME s-Flame, SPICE and SLICE.
The highest oxygen tested in any investigation, 40%, was with gas flames.

questions.question: Which experiments have full data tables?
paraphrases: Which studies have run-by-run data?
How complete is the PSI data for each experiment?
Which investigations recorded their test conditions?

answer.text: Eight investigations have run tables with conditions, eight have partial tables and three only a run log.
The full tables are BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I, SAFFIRE-II, FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, ACME Flame Design and ACME CFI-G.
BASS, DAFT / DAFT-2 and SLICE have only run logs.

questions.question: How much data does FlameMap use?
paraphrases: How many experiments are in FlameMap?
How many runs does the PSI data include?
What is in the FlameMap dataset?

answer.text: 19 flight investigations from NASA's PSI database, with 1993 experimental-table rows.
875 runs record both oxygen and pressure, and the records list 325 publications.

questions.question: What hardware did the experiments use?
paraphrases: Where on the space station were the fire experiments run?
Which experiments used the glovebox?
Which experiments flew on Cygnus?

answer.text: The ACME experiments, FLEX, FLEX-2 and CFI ran in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
BASS, BASS-II, SPICE, SAME and SAME-R used the station's glovebox.
SAFFIRE-I, SAFFIRE-II and SAFFIRE-III burned their samples inside Cygnus cargo vehicles.

questions.question: Has anything burned at high oxygen and low pressure?
paraphrases: Is there data at 30% oxygen and reduced pressure?
Which runs match a low-pressure, oxygen-rich habitat?
Any tests at high oxygen and 10 psi?

answer.text: 37 runs had at least 30% oxygen at 75 kPa or less: 20 from ACME CFI-G gas flames and 17 from FLEX droplets.
None of them burned a solid fuel.

questions.question: What is the lowest pressure any fire experiment tested?
paraphrases: Has anything been burned at low pressure?
What is the minimum cabin pressure tested in PSI?
Is there data below 70 kPa?

answer.text: 50.7 kPa, in FLEX-2 droplet tests; CFI and ACME CFI-G also reach 50.7 kPa.
No solid-fuel table records pressure at all.

questions.question: Which experiment has the most publications?
paraphrases: Which study is the most published?
Where is the most research literature?
Which investigation has the most papers?

answer.text: FLEX lists the most, 51 publications, followed by FLEX-2 with 48 and ACME s-Flame with 44.
Across all records PSI lists 325 publications.

questions.question: What were the Saffire experiments?
paraphrases: What is the Saffire program?
Tell me about the Saffire experiments
How big were the Saffire fires?

answer.text: SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III each burned one large cotton-fiberglass sample, about 0.94 m by 0.4 m and 94 cm by 40.6 cm, inside Cygnus cargo vehicles.
SAFFIRE-II burned 9 smaller samples of different materials on one card.
Their airflow ranged from 20 to 30 cm/s, and pressure is assumed to be cabin pressure.

questions.question: What is ACME?
paraphrases: What are the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments?
Which experiments are part of ACME?
What did the ACME gas flame experiments study?

answer.text: ACME (Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments) is a set of gas-flame investigations in the Combustion Integrated Rack: ACME BRE, Flame Design, CFI-G, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames and s-Flame.
ACME BRE is the one aimed directly at fire safety, emulating burning solids.

questions.question: What evidence applies to a Mars habitat?
paraphrases: Is there fire safety data for Mars?
Which experiments are closest to a Mars base?
How well is fire on Mars covered by tests?

answer.text: A Mars habitat at 30% oxygen and 70.3 kPa has the same gaps as a lunar one: the highest solid-fuel oxygen tested is 22.2%, and no solid-fuel table records pressure.
None of the 19 investigations ran at 0.38 g.
For materials, BASS-II and the Saffire flights come closest, all burned in microgravity.

questions.question: What evidence applies to the space station cabin?
paraphrases: Is there fire data for ISS conditions?
Which experiments match station cabin air?
How well tested is fire safety on the space station?

answer.text: The station cabin, at 21% oxygen and 101.3 kPa in microgravity, is the best-covered environment: 375 runs with both oxygen and pressure fall within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of it.
BASS-II, BASS and the three Saffire flights match it for materials, though their pressure is assumed rather than recorded.

questions.question: What evidence exists for the 10.2 psia Exploration Atmosphere?
paraphrases: Is there fire data for 26.5% oxygen?
How close are experiments to 26.5% oxygen at 70.3 kPa?
What about NASA's 10.2 psi atmosphere?

answer.text: It is the reduced-pressure atmosphere closest to tested solids: the highest solid-fuel oxygen, 22.2%, is 4.3 points below its 26.5%.
43 runs fall within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of it, all FLEX droplets.
As for every reduced-pressure atmosphere, no solid-fuel table records pressure, and nothing ran at lunar gravity.

questions.question: Does the PSI data apply to fires on Earth?
paraphrases: Can space fire research help on Earth?
Is there normal-gravity fire data in PSI?
How does this data relate to Earth fire safety?

answer.text: Only indirectly. All 19 investigations ran in microgravity, so none matches 1 g.
SAFFIRE-II is the exception: it lists 1-g comparison burns next to its microgravity results.

questions.question: Which experiments matter for fire detection in a lunar habitat?
paraphrases: How would we detect a fire on the Moon?
Is there smoke detection data for a Moon base?
Which smoke studies apply to a lunar habitat?

answer.text: SAME, SAME-R and DAFT / DAFT-2 rank highest, but all ran in assumed cabin air in microgravity, below the habitat's oxygen and above its pressure.
NASA notes that smoke particles from microgravity fires differ greatly in size from those on Earth, and no study measured smoke at lunar gravity.

questions.question: Which experiments matter for fire suppression in a lunar habitat?
paraphrases: How would we put out a fire on the Moon?
Is there extinguishment data for a Moon base?
Which suppression studies apply to a lunar habitat?

answer.text: FLEX and FLEX-2 rank highest: they recorded pressure ranges that include 70.3 kPa, and FLEX burned droplets at up to 34% oxygen.
FLEX found that inert-gas suppressant standards set on Earth give less safety margin in microgravity.
All of it is microgravity data; nothing ran at lunar gravity.

questions.question: Is a pressurized lunar rover different from a lunar habitat?
paraphrases: What about fire safety in a lunar rover?
Is there fire data for a pressurized rover?
Does the Moon rover atmosphere have any test data?

answer.text: Not in this data: the rover preset uses the same 30% oxygen, 70.3 kPa and 0.166 g as the lunar habitat, so its rankings and gaps are the same.
23 runs fall within 5 oxygen points and 10 kPa of it, all FLEX droplets, and none ran at lunar gravity.

questions.question: What are the biggest gaps in microgravity fire data?
paraphrases: What has never been tested in space fire research?
What fire experiments are still missing?
Where is the evidence weakest?

answer.text: No experiment ran at partial gravity: all 19 flight investigations ran in microgravity.
No solid fuel was burned above 22.2% oxygen, and no solid-fuel table records pressure.
Nothing comes near a spacesuit's 100% oxygen at 29.6 kPa; the highest oxygen in any table is 40%.
